exit_criterion: PROPOSAL.md section 16: "A non-developer on a clean machine downloads, installs and completes a PCA in under ten minutes." Concretely, and recorded rather than reasoned: a person who is not a developer, on a machine with no Python, Node or developer tools, is given only the release page and the documentation site, and is timed from the release page to the scores plot of a PCA on the example dataset. At least one run is on Windows. The maintainer arranges the session (decided 2026-09-28). The phase ends when that run is recorded in docs/phase-4/exit-run.md under ten minutes, and every obstacle it found is fixed or consciously accepted.
decisions: 2026-09-28. The exit run is done by a real non-developer the maintainer arranges; no automated stand-in replaces it.
2026-09-28. Packages ship unsigned at 1.0, with a 'How to open this' page for Gatekeeper and SmartScreen (PROPOSAL.md section 17's fallback).
2026-09-28. The documentation site is MkDocs Material, a development dependency only, published to GitHub Pages.
2026-09-28. Package formats: Windows .zip, macOS .dmg for Apple Silicon only, Linux .tar.gz. Intel macOS and AppImage are deferred.
2026-09-28. The name stays 'Chemometrics Workbench' for 1.0 (PROPOSAL.md section 19, question 3).

features.title: Localhost hardening: Host and Origin checked on every request
features.user_visible_behavior: None visible. A web page the user visits cannot reach the local server, by DNS rebinding or by a cross-origin request, and the development origins are no longer accepted by a packaged application.
verification: uv run pytest - a wrong Host and a foreign Origin are refused with a 403 in the error envelope on an API route and on the bundle; the Vite origins are accepted only in development mode; each test fails on the unfixed code first
The path audit: every endpoint listed with what it takes from the client, showing none accepts a server-side path
pnpm exec playwright test - the application still works through its own origin
features.evidence: 2026-09-28. `uv run pytest`: `910 passed, 1 skipped`. tests/test_server.py has one test per section 4.3 requirement. A `Host` of `attacker.example:8765` is refused 403 `forbidden` on `/api/projects`, `/` and `/index.html`, and both loopback names are accepted with or without a port. A foreign `Origin` (`http://attacker.example`, `http://127.0.0.1:9999`, `http://localhost:5173`, `null`) is refused even with the token, and the application's own origin or none is accepted. `http://localhost:5173` is accepted only with `DEV` set, and a preflight gets no `access-control-allow-origin`. No response sets a cookie and a cookie is not a token. `main()` binds `127.0.0.1` on port 0. Proof: against dev's server.py with the new tests kept, the Host, Origin and dev-origin tests FAILED; the cookie and bind tests passed on both, as they guard requirements already met. A real uvicorn process probed with curl: production gives own Origin 200, `localhost:5173` 403, rebound Host 403, no Origin 200; `WORKBENCH_DEV=1` gives `localhost:5173` 200 and everything else unchanged. `pnpm exec playwright test`: `61 passed (2.5m)`; the browser sends its own Origin on every write. Path audit, every route in api.py: the project directory comes from the environment, never from a request; an upload's filename is reduced to `Path(...).name` inside a fresh temporary directory; stored arrays and results are named by content-hash keys, and `node_id`, `experiment_id`, `job_id` and `model_id` are only looked up, never joined into a path; a saved model's file is `models/<uuid>.cwmodel`, generated server-side. No endpoint accepts a server-side path. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` clean.
features.notes: PROPOSAL.md section 4.3. Already met before this phase: 127.0.0.1 only, an ephemeral port, a per-session bearer token compared in constant time, no cookies, and bundle paths confined to the bundle. Missing: Host and Origin validation, and DEV_ORIGINS gated to development.

features.title: A launcher: double-click, the browser opens on the workbench
features.user_visible_behavior: Starting the application opens the default browser on the workbench, already authenticated, with the default project open; a console window says how to stop it.
verification: uv run pytest - the URL handed to the browser carries the bound port and the token; the bundle is found from a simulated frozen layout; two launches get two ports
Started from a checkout, the browser opens on the workbench with no terminal input
features.evidence: 2026-09-29. `uv run pytest`: `913 passed, 1 skipped`. tests/test_server.py adds three tests. Two real launches of `main(open_browser=True)` run side by side on threads: each hands the browser `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?token=<token>` with its own bound port (the two differ and equal the sockets' ports), and each URL answers `/api/projects` 200 by the time the browser is told of it. `main()` without the flag opens nothing, which is what Playwright, seed_e2e and the exit runs start. With `sys.frozen` and `sys._MEIPASS` set to a directory holding `frontend/dist/index.html`, `BUNDLE` resolves there and `/` serves it. Proof: against dev's server.py with the new tests kept, all three FAILED. From a checkout, `python -m chemometrics_workbench` (what `./run.sh` now execs) with `BROWSER` set to a script that records its argument, since that is what `webbrowser` hands any browser: it received `http://127.0.0.1:45515/?token=...` with no terminal input; that URL served `<title>Chemometrics Workbench`, `/api/projects` with its token answered 200, the console printed "Close this window to stop the workbench.", and `<config dir>/projects/default` was created. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` clean.
features.notes: PROPOSAL.md sections 4.1 and 4.2. server.py prints the launch URL today and nothing opens it. The project already defaults to <config dir>/projects/default when CHEMOMETRICS_PROJECT is unset. Done as `python -m chemometrics_workbench` (`__main__.py`), which is also what PyInstaller should take as its entry script; `python -m chemometrics_workbench.server` stays serve-only. `webbrowser.open` runs on a daemon thread: called on the event loop, a browser that blocks (a console browser, or the test's fetching stand-in) held the loop that has to answer it.
